sentences.text: After successful operator authentication, Atlas Onboard Controller assumes the active train control role when the train is energized and train integrity indications are valid.
The Atlas Onboard Controller is referred to in some installation drawings as Kestrel, but this document uses Atlas Onboard Controller as the canonical name.
Atlas Onboard Controller supervises movement authority processing, onboard speed enforcement, door enable logic, and train interface commands required for CBTC operation.
The controller maintains a safety-critical state machine that separates initialization, protected manual operation, automatic train operation, fallback operation, and cutout conditions.
Movement authority data received from North District Zone Controller and South District Zone Controller is checked for sequence, applicability, and consistency before it is applied onboard.
Interlocking indications associated with East Junction Interlocking and West Junction Interlocking are treated as wayside state inputs conveyed through established safety channels.
Dual Channel Odometer provides independent speed and distance measurements derived from axle rotation, inertial sensing, and configured calibration parameters.
Atlas Onboard Controller compares the two odometry channels continuously and degrades the operating mode when the measured divergence exceeds the permitted threshold.
When odometry confidence is reduced, the onboard functions increase position uncertainty and request operating actions that preserve separation from other trains.
The trainborne interface to propulsion and braking equipment converts safety commands into vehicle-compatible requests while preserving electrical isolation from non-vital circuits.
Brake assurance functions verify service and emergency brake availability by monitoring brake feedback, pneumatic pressure indications, and commanded deceleration response.
During each enforcement cycle, Atlas Onboard Controller recalculates the braking demand needed to keep the train within the authorized movement limits.
Atlas Onboard Controller produces the Brake Curve Checksum Log after validating the active enforcement data set.
Train Radio Modem provides the onboard data radio function and maintains CBTC sessions over Wayside Radio Access Network coverage areas.
The radio subsystem reports link quality, registration state, and session continuity information to Atlas Onboard Controller for use in mode management.
Safety Data Communication Network provides the protected communications transport used by train control messages that require integrity, authentication, and bounded latency.
Safety Data Communication Network sends the Clock Drift Sample Report at defined synchronization intervals.
Cryptographic Key Management Appliance supports the security material used by onboard communications without changing the safety logic executed on the train.
The operator interface presents movement authority limits, permitted speed, train location confidence, radio condition, and required operator actions to Revenue Train Operator.
Acknowledgements entered by Revenue Train Operator are passed to Atlas Onboard Controller through a monitored input path that rejects stale or inconsistent commands.
Voice Dispatch Console remains operationally separate from the vital CBTC data path, but it provides a means for voice coordination during degraded service.
Platform Screen Door Controller exchanges door enable and closed-and-locked indications with the train interface when the train is correctly berthed at a platform.
Passenger Information Gateway receives non-vital train position and service state data through an interface that prevents passenger systems from influencing safety decisions.
Service Timetable Server provides schedule context to Metro Operations Control System and related non-vital functions, while onboard enforcement remains based on safety authority and train state.
The Maintenance Diagnostic Server is referred to in some maintenance work instructions as Quarry, but this document uses Maintenance Diagnostic Server as the canonical name.

Maintenance Diagnostic Server collects non-vital health indications from trainborne equipment so that Signal Maintenance Engineer can review faults without connecting directly to vital processing functions.
